title: A report naming one check twice reached persistence, where PostgreSQL refused it on the primary key while the in-memory store accepted it, so a report with a failed result could leave an earlier admitted state
resolution: The decision stores a check named more than once as one failed result, so no repeat reaches a store and such a report never admits; the AsyncAPI description, contract section 4a, and the spec say so. Tests: equal and conflicting repeats in the decision, both stores, the service, and the NATS reader.

title: The worker kept only the first eight checks in identifier order, so a failing ninth check could be left out of a passing report
resolution: checkComposition refuses more than eight checks, a repeated id, or a malformed id; startWorker calls it before enrollment and runSelfCheck returns the failure. The truncation test is replaced by tests that a ninth check is refused before any check runs and that the start fails before enrollment.

title: The test for a running execution through a failed self-check created no execution, grant, or start before the report
resolution: The test now authorizes and starts an execution before the failed report, then asserts the kept ownership, held reservation, granted grant, started state, no cancellation or assignment end, a supersession refused with precondition-failed, and a normal exit that ends the task.

title: The scenario stored an unrecognised not-applicable reason as failed, although the wire schema refuses such a report before the decision, so it is quarantined and changes nothing
resolution: Scenario Malformed reason: the schema refuses the report, which is quarantined with the admission unchanged; a valid reason the enrolled platform refutes is stored as failed. Contract section 4a, the wire contract, and design D3a agree; a NATS reader test covers the refusal.

title: The shared conformance suite had no case for a workers view whose source cannot be read, which contract section 9 requires
resolution: The fixture gains breakWorker, and a shared case requires unavailable with no partial data; the PostgreSQL view maps an unreadable enrollment record to unavailable. The in-memory run passes; the PostgreSQL run awaits the coordinator's make verify.

title: The requirement placed running the checks after the capacity declaration, while the worker runs them before it and only journals the report after capacity and pressure
resolution: The requirement now says the checks run before the broker session and the report is journaled after the capacity declaration and the pressure report, as design D2 and startRuntime do.

title: The wire contract's document table still gave the execution AsyncAPI version as 0.6.0
The record cited the supersession due check as the protection of granted assignments, although that check is due for any worker that is not admitted and the grant guard is in supersedeAssignment
resolution: The author self-check now separates due (isSupersessionDue) from allowed: supersedeAssignment refuses an assignment with a granted execution, and the execution only ends through its terminal fact.

title: The launch authority did not check worker admission, so a worker that is not admitted still got new grants for assignments it had accepted
resolution: A new operation of a worker that is not admitted is refused with the existing non-retryable worker-not-authorized, after the installation and worker checks; replays are not gated. Contract sections 4a and 7 state the self-attested trust model; a new requirement and a fail-before test cover it.

title: An accepted assignment without a grant on a worker whose self-check failed was never freed, because nothing in production acts on the due supersession
resolution: The report that makes the worker self-check-failed frees each unfinished assignment without a grant through freeIdleAssignment and keeps granted ones; D6, contract section 7, and the scenario say due at once and freed; a fail-before test covers it.

title: Design D7 justified protocol version 1 with a worker of this build, while the cited rule concerns a worker that supports neither version
resolution: D7 now speaks of an older build that sends no report, and wire contract section 3 states that a worker without a self-check report is never admitted.

title: The deferred-resume log reason said no launch command although a failed self-check also removes the launch authority
resolution: The log reason is no launch authority and the comment names both causes; the offline launch test expects the new reason.

title: No test showed that the migration leaves existing workers awaiting their self-check
resolution: A held-migration test inserts a worker first and asserts awaiting-self-check, fence 0, no report time, and no eligibility; it awaits the coordinator's make verify.

title: The journal adapter's new self-check fact had no spec delta beside the matching admission pressure requirement
resolution: A worker-journal-adapter delta adds Self-check report facts with a scenario of two reports with distinct identities, covered by the existing journal test; the proposal lists the capability.

title: The requirement said an invalid composition fails the start before enrollment, which means nothing for an enrolled worker
resolution: The requirement and its scenario say before it enrolls or opens its journal, as the contract does.

title: The record cited a running-execution test by its name before a rename
resolution: The record gives the current name and notes the earlier one.

title: The record did not include the coordinator's passing make verify on the pass 1 head and still listed it as a gate
resolution: The run on 9c849c02 is recorded with its totals, and the limitation and gate now concern only the head after pass 2.

title: A failed self-check report skipped by the sequence fence still freed the assignments of an admitted worker
resolution: WorkerAdmissions.record answers applied or fenced in both adapters, and assignments are freed only for an applied failed report; a regression test and a conformance case cover it. Fixed without another review by the away-delegate decision of 2026-10-28.
